text: An ideal gas is enclosed in a cylinder at pressure of 2 atm and temperature 300 K. The mean time between two successive collisions is 6 $\times$ $10^{–8} s$. If the pressure is doubled and temperature is increased to 500 K, the mean time between two successive collisions will be close to
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mean time between two successive collisions is the mean free path divided by the average speed of the molecules:

$τ=\frac{λ}{\bar{v}},λ=\frac{k_{B}T}{\sqrt{2}πd^{2}P},\bar{v}=\sqrt{\frac{8k_{B}T}{πm}}.$

So $λ\propto \dfrac{T}{P}$ and $\bar{v}\propto \sqrt{T}$, which gives

$τ\propto \frac{T/P}{\sqrt{T}}=\frac{\sqrt{T}}{P}.$

With $P_{2}=2P_{1}$, $T_{1}=300\text{K}$ and $T_{2}=500\text{K}$:

$\frac{τ_{2}}{τ_{1}}=\sqrt{\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}}\times \frac{P_{1}}{P_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{500}{300}}\times \frac{1}{2}\approx \frac{1.29}{2}\approx 0.65$

$τ_{2}\approx 0.65\times 6\times 10^{-8}\text{s}\approx 3.9\times 10^{-8}\text{s}\approx 4\times 10^{-8}\text{s}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text: The moment of inertia of a solid sphere, about an axis parallel to its diameter and at a distance of x from it, is 'I(x)'. Which one of the graphs represents the variation of I(x) with x correctly ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The correct answer is Option C. Here's why :

The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about an axis passing through its center is given by :

$I_{0}=\frac{2}{5}MR^{2}$

Where :

  $I_{0}$ is the moment of inertia about the center

  $M$ is the mass of the sphere

  $R$ is the radius of the sphere

Now, using the parallel axis theorem, we can find the moment of inertia about an axis parallel to the diameter and at a distance of 'x' from it :

$I(x)=I_{0}+Mx^{2}$

Substituting the value of $I_{0}$ :

$I(x)=\frac{2}{5}MR^{2}+Mx^{2}$

This equation represents a parabola, where :

 The coefficient of $x^{2}$ is positive (M), indicating an upward-opening parabola.

  The y-intercept (the value of $I(x)$ when $x=0$) is $\frac{2}{5}MR^{2}$, which is a positive constant.

Therefore, the graph of $I(x)$ vs. $x$ should be an upward-opening parabola, and Option C accurately represents this.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text:
In the given circuit diagram, the currents, $I_{1} = – 0.3 A, I_{4} = 0.8 A$ and $I_{5} = 0.4 A$, are flowing as shown. The  currents $I_{2}, I_{3}$ and $I_{6}$, respectively, are :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
By Kirchhoff's junction law, no charge accumulates at a junction in the steady state, so $\sum I_{\text{in}}=\sum I_{\text{out}}$ at every node.


[IMG]


At node $P$, the current $I_{5}$ comes in and $I_{6}$ goes out, so $I_{5}=I_{6}\Rightarrow I_{6}=0.4\mathrm{A}$.

At node $S$, the current $I_{4}$ comes in and the currents $I_{5}$ and $I_{3}$ go out, so $I_{4}=I_{5}+I_{3}\Rightarrow I_{3}=I_{4}-I_{5}$.

With the given values $I_{4}=0.8\mathrm{A}$ and $I_{5}=0.4\mathrm{A}$, $I_{3}=0.8\mathrm{A}-0.4\mathrm{A}=0.4\mathrm{A}$.

At node $Q$, the currents $I_{6}$ and $I_{3}$ come in and the currents $I_{2}$ and $I_{1}$ go out, so $I_{6}+I_{3}=I_{2}+I_{1}\Rightarrow I_{2}=I_{6}+I_{3}-I_{1}$.

Substituting $I_{6}=0.4\mathrm{A}$, $I_{3}=0.4\mathrm{A}$ and $I_{1}=-0.3\mathrm{A}$,

$I_{2}=0.4\mathrm{A}+0.4\mathrm{A}-(-0.3\mathrm{A})=0.8\mathrm{A}+0.3\mathrm{A}=1.1\mathrm{A}$

As a check, at node $R$ the currents $I_{2}$ and $I_{1}$ come in and $I_{4}$ goes out, and indeed $I_{2}+I_{1}=1.1\mathrm{A}-0.3\mathrm{A}=0.8\mathrm{A}=I_{4}$.

Therefore, the unknown currents are $I_{2}=1.1\mathrm{A}$, $I_{3}=0.4\mathrm{A}$ and $I_{6}=0.4\mathrm{A}$.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
A load of mass M kg is suspended from a steel wire of length 2m and radius 1.0 mm in Searle's apparatus
experiment. The increase in length produced in the wire is 4.0 mm. Now the load is fully immersed in a liquid of relative density 2. The relative density of the material of load is 8. 

The new value of increase in length of the steel wire is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In Searle's experiment the extension of the wire is $\Delta \ell =\dfrac{T\ell }{AY}$, so for the same wire $\Delta \ell \propto T$.

In air the tension is $T=Mg$.


[IMG]

When the load is fully immersed, the buoyant force is $f_{B}=Vρ_{\ell }g=\dfrac{M}{ρ_{b}}ρ_{\ell }g$, so the new tension is

$T^{'}=Mg-f_{B}=Mg\left (1-\dfrac{ρ_{\ell }}{ρ_{b}}\right )=Mg\left (1-\dfrac{2}{8}\right )=\dfrac{3}{4}Mg$

The new extension is

$\Delta \ell ^{'}=\dfrac{T^{'}}{T}\Delta \ell =\dfrac{3}{4}\times 4.0\text{mm}=3.0\text{mm}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text: A resonance tube is old and has jagged end. It is still used in the laboratory to determine velocity of sound in air. A tuning fork of frequency 512 Hz produces first resonance when the tube is filled with water to a mark 11 cm below a reference mark, near the open end of the tube. The experiment is repeated with another fork of frequency 256 Hz which produces first resonance when water reaches a mark 27 cm below the reference mark. The velocity of sound in air, obtained in the experiment, is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A resonance tube is a pipe closed at one end (by the water surface) and open at the other end.
For a pipe closed at one end, a displacement node is at the closed end (water surface) and a displacement antinode is near the open end.
At the fundamental frequency (first resonance), $L_{\text{eff}}=\dfrac{λ}{4}$
Since wave velocity $v$, frequency $f$, and wavelength $λ$ are related as $v=fλ\Rightarrow λ=\dfrac{v}{f}$
Substituting $λ$ into the condition for the first resonance, $L_{\text{eff}}=\dfrac{v}{4f}\ldots (\text{i})$
Because the open end is jagged, the antinode does not lie exactly at the reference mark. Let $x$ be the unknown distance of the antinode above the reference mark (it includes the end correction), so the effective length of the air column is $L_{\text{eff}}=l+x$, where $l$ is the length of the air column measured below the reference mark.
For the first tuning fork, the resonant frequency is $f_{1}=512\mathrm{Hz}$ and resonant column length is $l_{1}=11\mathrm{cm}=0.11\mathrm{m}$.

[IMG]

$L_{\text{eff}(1)}=\frac{v}{4\times 512}=\frac{v}{2048}=0.11+x\ldots (\text{ii})$
For the second tuning fork, the resonant frequency is $f_{2}=256\mathrm{Hz}$ and resonant column length is $l_{2}=27\mathrm{cm}=0.27\mathrm{m}$.

[IMG]

$L_{\text{eff}(2)}=\frac{v}{4\times 256}=\frac{v}{1024}=0.27+x\ldots (\text{iii})$
On subtracting equation (ii) from equation (iii), the unknown $x$ cancels:
$\Rightarrow 0.27-0.11=\frac{v}{1024}-\frac{v}{2048}$
$\Rightarrow 0.16=\frac{2v-v}{2048}=\frac{v}{2048}\Rightarrow v=0.16\times 2048$
$v\approx 328\mathrm{m}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$
Therefore, the velocity of sound in air is approximately $328\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$.
Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

text: A soap bubble, blown by a mechanical pump at the mouth of a tube, increases in volume, with time, at a constant rate. The graph that correctly depicts the time dependence of pressure inside the bubble is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When soap bubble is being inflated and its temperature remains constant, then it follows Boyle's law, so

pV = constant (k)

$\Rightarrow p=\frac{k}{V}$

Differentiating above equation with time, we get

$\frac{dp}{dt}=k.\frac{d}{dt}\left (\frac{1}{V}\right )$

$\Rightarrow \frac{dp}{dt}=k\left (\frac{-1}{V^{2}}\right ).\frac{dV}{dt}$

It is given that, $\frac{dV}{dt}=c$ (a constant)

So, $\frac{dp}{dt}=\frac{-kc}{V^{2}}$ ..... (i)

Now, from $\frac{dV}{dt}=c$, we get

$dV=cdt$

or, $\int dV=\int cdt$ or, $V=ct$ ..... (ii)

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get

$\frac{dp}{dt}=\frac{-kc}{c^{2}t^{2}}$

or, $\frac{dp}{dt}=-\left (\frac{k}{c}\right )t^{-2}$

$\Rightarrow dp=-\frac{k}{c}.t^{-2}dt$

Integrating both sides, we get

$\int dp=-\frac{k}{c}\int t^{-2}dt$

$p=-\frac{k}{c}.\left (\frac{t^{-2+1}}{-2+1}\right )$

$=-\frac{k}{c}.\frac{-1}{t}=\frac{k}{ct}$

or, $p\propto \frac{1}{t}$

Hence, p versus $\frac{1}{t}$ graph is a straight line, which is correctly represented in option (b).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Evening Slot

solution.body:
Phase difference between $I_{2}$ and V, i.e. C $-$ $R_{2}$ circuit is given by

$\tan 𝜙=\frac{X_{C}}{R_{2}}\Rightarrow \tan 𝜙=\frac{1}{CωR_{2}}$

Substituting the given values, we get

$\tan 𝜙=\frac{1}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times 10^{-6}\times 100\times 20}=\frac{10^{3}}{\sqrt{3}}$

$\therefore$ $𝜙_{1}$ is nearly 90${}^{\circ }$.

Phase difference between $I_{1}$ and V, i.e. in L $-$ $R_{1}$ circuit is given by

$\tan 𝜙_{2}=-\frac{X_{L}}{R_{1}}=-\frac{Lω}{R}$

Substituting the given values, we get

$\tan 𝜙_{2}=-\frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{10}\times 100}{10}=-\sqrt{3}$

As, $\tan 𝜙_{2}=-\sqrt{3}$

$\therefore$ $𝜙_{2}=120^{\circ }$

Now, phase difference between $I_{1}$ and $I_{2}$ is

$\Delta 𝜙=𝜙_{2}-𝜙_{1}=120^{\circ }-90^{\circ }=30^{\circ }$
